answer: Anchor each agent to a unique human through a one-shot biometric proof-of-personhood: a live iris scan is hashed to a template and deduplicated against every prior enrollment, so a second agent claiming the same person collides and is rejected. A farm can spawn clones as plentiful as sparrows for nearly free, yet each still needs a distinct living person to clear a liveness check: you cannot fool the pulse-and-motion test with a marble bust or a scrap of velvet draped over the lens. The scarce, non-forgeable cost is real humans, not GPUs.
